title: Mutes, rumbas and hotel dance work
summary: The band could not carry mutes for sweet music and played rumbas on hotel jobs; sweet bands ruled the North.

story.theme_name: Playing for dancers: dance bands and the dances themselves
story.community_name: Dancing to the band: quadrilles, waltzes and dance sets

blocks.x: So in fact, you preferred to play gigs where you cut loose.

Uh-huh. Because they had different kinds of mutes in the trumpets and things, to get all that beautiful music. And them boys didn't have it. They wasn't buying them kind of mutes and things to get that pretty sound. They had two or three little mutes for Jazz or something like that. But all that pretty stuff they wasn't buying, because we'd mostly play one night here, and then we were going somewhere the next night...
You couldn't carry all that stuff with you.
No. We couldn't keep up with it.
And what other sort of straight dances were there? Waltzes. What else would you be expected to play?

Yeah. We had to do a lot of that. Especially when you'd get playing on these hotel jobs. In the Trianon Ballroom you had to play a lot that way. Up in South Dakota, back through Illinois. Because them bands came out of that way, King...and I can't think of that other band. [JAN GARBER?] Anyway, they was all sweet bands, and that was their territory, right through that way. They would hardly ever come down this way.
